changes: Added the no-x86 host_gpu_native_b1_core plus extracted HostNativeQueueCore and HostNativeCommandProcessorCore while leaving the legacy AMDGPU SimObject sources unchanged.
Reused CP17/CP18 staging, address, descriptor, kernarg, AQL, MQD, lifecycle, and HSAQueueEntry contracts to publish, ring, fetch, and admit one locked gfx950 packet through the native cores.

Recorded aql_submitted_to_native_core=true (EV-0046: aql_submitted_to_native_cp_core=true) while legacy_gpu_pipeline_submitted, cu_wave_started, instruction_fetched, hsa_packet_retired, signal_decremented, and kernel_executed remain false.
Added queue-wrap, skipped-ring, malformed-MQD, malformed-packet, in-flight-unregister, ordering, and explicit no-retire/no-signal/no-CU boundary checks.
Retained the CP15-CP18 host-native checkers, four boundary tests, eight VEGA_X86 compatibility regressions, pinned Qwen model hashes, and the 15/15 static operator gate.
limitations: CP-0019-B1 aql_submitted is scoped to acceptance by the extracted HostNativeCommandProcessorCore. It is not submission through the legacy HSAPP/GPUCommandProcessor SimObjects or gem5 GPU pipeline.
The no-x86 B1 target does not link or instantiate legacy HSAPP, GPUCommandProcessor, GPUDispatcher, ComputeUnit, Shader, AMDGPUDevice, System, Process, ThreadContext, x86 ISA, or x86 CPU objects.

B1 does not update the host-visible MQD read index, retire the AQL packet, decrement its completion signal, start a CU wave, fetch or retire an instruction, execute gfx950 ISA, or compare kernel output. Those are B2 boundaries.

The locked zero-relocation gpuReadWrite image, fixed kernarg ABI, queue geometry, and host-owned address ledger are not a generic arbitrary-ELF loader, relocation/permission proof, legacy GPU VM/TLB proof, or transparent runtime launcher.

Qwen3.5-0.8B evidence remains offline model/hash and static 15-contract source/shape preparation; strict AMD execution is blocked by the detected CUDA/NVIDIA environment, CPU/NVIDIA fallback is not a pass, and inference remains 0/1.
The retained Triton overlay remains compile-only historical provenance; Triton end-to-end remains 0/1, with no full ROCm/OpenCL CTS, HIP/OpenCL/PyTorch/vLLM, hardware, timing, or performance claim.
